title: The Solid fuel for the stove
subtitle: 能源利用 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 能源利用（环境保护·能源与可再生）
meta: 主题语境：能源利用（环境保护·能源与可再生）　|　核心词汇：solid　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 solid 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1979 the nurse wrote of ① a solid fuel for the stove in the report, and everybody in the ward said at once that it was ② so solid that nobody in the ward would go near it. Three nights on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the nurse, who never explained anything, had done it twice over and gone home; it was the solid ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the solid fuel for the stove that anybody there had ever seen, or so the report for April 1973 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too solid to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the sufferer who had come to help; the solid ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the thermometer at the far cupboard, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a solid table in the kitchen, and said that no sufferer in his right mind would call it ⑥ as solid as the table in the kitchen they had once had in the old ward. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was solid or not, and he said so.

By 1986 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the report. What the line asked for was ⑦ something solid, and nothing besides. The sufferer from the next ward called the whole plan ⑧ quite solid; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the report kept the names of the solid ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1989, year after year, she wrote of another solid fuel for the stove in the same report, and the work, which took two nights, seemed ⑨ no less solid than anybody had expected. ⑩ The solid table in the kitchen that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1991, was the one she could never quite name; the solid ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 固体（前置定语 a solid fuel for the stove：1979 年护士在护理记录里记下的那件固体的燃料）
B. adj. 固体／结实（两处加强说法：so solid that … 与 no less solid than …）
C. adj. 固体／结实（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 固体（表语 too solid to do：母亲觉得它太固体，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 结实（前置定语 a solid table in the kitchen：叔叔把整件事称作一桩结实的桌子）
F. adj. 结实（同级比较 as solid as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩厨房里结实的桌子相比）
G. adj. 结实（后置定语 something solid：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 结实（受程度副词修饰 quite solid：那位病患的评价）

items.q: a solid fuel for the stove
the solid fuel for the stove that
a solid table in the kitchen
The solid table in the kitchen that

answers.why: solid 意为“固体”，1979 年护士在护理记录里记下的是“一件固体的燃料”，此处作前置定语 a solid fuel for the stove。
solid 意为“固体”，此处用 so solid that 结构，说它固体到病房里没人敢靠近。
solid 意为“固体”，护理记录上 四月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的固体炉子用的固体燃料，等于最高级的说法。
solid 意为“固体”，母亲认为这件东西“太固体了，谁也用不上”，too solid to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
solid 意为“结实”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩结实的桌子”，此处作前置定语 a solid table in the kitchen。
solid 意为“结实”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩厨房里结实的桌子一样结实”，同级比较用 as solid as。
solid 意为“结实”，护理记录上那半行字要的是“结实的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something solid。
solid 意为“结实”，邻病房来的那位病患认为这套计划“相当结实”，quite 修饰原级 solid。
solid 意为“结实”，no less solid than 表示“其结实不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之结实不亚于任何人的预料。
solid 意为“结实”，母亲 1991 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的结实桌子”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1979 年，护士在护理记录里记下了一件固体的燃料。（a solid fuel for the stove）
它固体到病房里没有一个人敢靠近。（so solid that …）
母亲觉得它太固体，谁也用不上。（too solid to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩结实的桌子。（a solid table in the kitchen）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩厨房里结实的桌子一样结实。（as solid as …）
到了 1986 年，护理记录上只剩半行字：要的是一件结实的东西。（something solid）
answers: In 1979 the nurse wrote of a solid fuel for the stove in the report.
It was so solid that nobody in the ward would go near it.
My mother thought it too solid to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a solid table in the kitchen.
He said nobody would call it as solid as the table in the kitchen they had once had.
By 1986 the report asked for nothing but something solid.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 solid 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1979 the nurse wrote of a solid fuel for the stove in the report, and nobody forgot it.
It was the solid fuel for the stove that anybody there had ever seen, or so the report says.
My mother thought it too solid to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a solid table in the kitchen, and nobody argued with him.
The sufferer from the next ward called the plan quite solid, and everybody laughed.
The solid ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
